concept: One long whiteboard that runs through a single invented incident: moving right is moving forward through the lesson and the night, moving down is looking closer (at the engineer, under the rule, into the system). The meeting room drawn from above opens and closes the film with the same geometry, first with every head on the engineer, finally with every head on the board. Motifs: the room's turning heads, the engineer's thought bubble, and the three invented conditions, which appear on the timeline, converge as arrows, become the quiz, stand beside the struck card, turn into owned fixes and end up on the board.

design.treatment: Late night at a desk, side view, whiteboard sketch. Left half: the on-call engineer (peep woman, cloth accent2) at an open laptop, a window with a crescent moon behind. Right half: a sketched panel for the made-up online store with a live orders line that ticks along steadily, then drops and runs flat. No numbers, no axis values, no times anywhere (the knowledge sheet has none, and the incident is invented).
design.why_motion: The incident is an event: a change goes out and a running flow of orders stops. The line changing from ticking to flat IS what the viewer must see; a still of a flat line would not show that it was running a second ago.
elements: desk: desk line, open laptop, window with a moon icon, x 120-900, y 260-900
engineer: peep woman, cloth accent2, seated at the laptop; neutral, swaps to surprised at the flatline
change_tag: small sticky tag on the laptop screen reading 'Routine change', with a rocket icon as the deploy button
store_panel: sketched panel x 1040-1800, y 240-760, header 'Online store' with a store icon, a baseline and an empty plot area (no axis labels)
orders_line: hand-drawn line inside store_panel, small label 'Orders' at its left end
incident_note (MOTIF via ctx.motif('incident_note', ...)): stamp-style note 'Orders stopped' with a shopping-cart icon, x 1180-1660, y 790-890; b02 adopts it

beat_sheet.action: desk reveals, engineer settles 0.1 s after it
drops onto the laptop screen; the rocket button presses (scale 1 to 0.92 to 1)
panel assembles left to right, then the orders line starts drawing left to right with small regular ticks (running flow)
the line falls to the baseline and runs flat (about 0.8 s, ease-out); engineer swaps to surprised as it lands
stamps the instant the line is flat (delay = the flatline's own duration, from the same setting)

design.continuity: Creates the motif incident_note, which b02 adopts and flies onto the room's whiteboard during the travel join. Everything else retires.

scenes.rationale: Hook: the invented incident as one event, flow then flat. 'Say' framing is in the narration.

design.treatment: The meeting room from above, plan-view whiteboard sketch filling the frame. Room geometry (shared with b28, which must redraw it identically): walls x 100-1860, y 90-900 with a door gap on the bottom wall at x 300-420; oval table centred (800,500), 760x300, hachure fill surface2; six heads (top-down: a hachured hair disc r 44 with a small nose tick showing facing) at (480,330), (800,300), (1120,330), (1120,670), (800,700) and the engineer at (470,660); the whiteboard face-on along the right wall at x 1440-1840, y 180-780 (surface fill, ink frame). The engineer's head carries an accent2 ring (the same colour as b01's cloth) and a small label 'engineer'. At the end every head points at the engineer and the frame holds, frozen.
design.why_motion: The room's attention moving onto one person is the hook's content. Watching the heads swing, one by one, is the feeling the lesson is about; a still of heads already turned would lose the turn.
